# Booked rooms nobody turns up to are freed for others

## Description

Booked rooms in the London, Manchester and Leeds offices often sit empty because nobody turns up. When this initiative is done, each room with a tablet by its door shows that room's bookings for today. People check in there from 5 minutes before a booking starts until 15 minutes after. A booking nobody checks into by then is freed: the rest of its slot becomes bookable by anyone, and its organiser sees it as freed. Office managers see how many bookings their office freed this week. It changes how bookings end in the existing room booker, which today deletes a booking to stop it blocking its slot. The request and the answers that shaped it are in `sources/request-2026-11-13.md`. How bookings end today is in the booking-lifecycle research.

## Outcome

Rooms that were booked and then abandoned go back to people who need them. The signal: in a room with a tablet set up, an unclaimed booking is freed 15 minutes after its start, someone else can book the rest of the slot, and the office manager's weekly count goes up by one (S15: no numeric target this release).

## Requirements

- R1 (S4, S9): An office manager sets up a tablet once for one room in their office; from then on the tablet shows that room's page with no further sign-in.
- R2 (S4): The room's tablet page shows that room's bookings for today (UK day), and which one is current or next.
- R3 (S5, S11): Anyone at the tablet checks in a booking with one tap, without saying who they are, from 5 minutes before its start until 15 minutes after; outside that window the tablet offers no check-in for it.
- R4 (S3, S6): A booking with no check-in by 15 minutes after its start is freed: the rest of its slot, from 15 minutes after its start to its end, can be booked by anyone like any free time.
- R5 (S6, S12): A freed booking shows as "Freed: nobody checked in" on its organiser's My bookings and on its details page, and as cancelled in their subscribed calendar; it is distinct from a booking that was cancelled or simply ended.
- R6 (S7, S14): An office manager sees, beside their office's rooms on Manage rooms, how many bookings in their office were freed from Monday to today, UK time.
- R7 (S13): A booking in a room whose tablet has not been set up is never freed.

## Constraints

- C1 (S8): No QR codes, sensors, badges or notifications in this release.
- C2 (S9): The tablets are ordinary tablets showing a web page of the app; no native app or device management.
- C3 (S10; research §1, §3): Today a booking stops blocking its slot only when its row is deleted, since the overlap guard counts every row, and nothing records how a booking ended. Freeing must keep `bookings.service`'s write lock and the overlap triggers as the double-booking guarantee (AGENTS.md).
- C4 (S10; research §1, §5): Python reads time from `core.time.utc_now()` while SQLite triggers read their own clock, and tests cannot fake it. Release must be testable at its boundary, 15 minutes after the start exactly.
- C5 (AGENTS.md): Every page, the tablet's included, works as a full page load; htmx only narrows the swap.
- C6 (S12; research §2): Subscribed calendar feeds today drop cancelled bookings and key events by a UID hashing room, start, end and title. Showing a booking as freed there must not re-create or break other events in existing subscriptions.

## Done when

- A tablet set up by an office manager shows its room's bookings for today and checks one in within the window, and only within it.
- A booking nobody checks into is freed 15 minutes after its start, and someone else can then book the rest of its slot; a checked-in booking, or one in a room with no tablet set up, is never freed.
- The organiser sees a freed booking as freed on My bookings, its details page and their subscribed calendar.
- An office manager sees this week's freed count for their office on Manage rooms.
- Live in production for all three offices.

## Boundaries

- Out: QR codes, sensors, badges, notifications of any kind (C1).
- Out: booking a room from the tablet; the tablet only shows today's bookings and checks them in.
- Out: knowing who checked in; check-in is anonymous (S11).
- Out: a numeric target for freed bookings this release (S15).
- Touch point: rooms — which rooms have a tablet set up, and the freed count on Manage rooms.
- Touch point: bookings — check-in, freeing, and what freed means for overlap and listings.
- Touch point: calendar — My bookings and the subscribed feed show freed bookings.
- Must not change: how a booking is made, cancelled, or removed by closing its room; the overlap guarantee; rooms with no tablet behave exactly as today.
- Tracer path: an office manager sets up a room's tablet; a booking in that room passes 15 minutes after its start with no check-in; it is freed; someone else books the rest of the slot; the organiser sees it as freed; the manager's weekly count shows it.

## References

- source — _bmad-output/initiative-check-in/sources/request-2026-11-13.md, S1–S15
- research — _bmad-output/research-booking-lifecycle-and-end/research-booking-lifecycle-and-end.md, §1 (how bookings end), §2 (what reads end time), §3 (triggers), §5 (time in tests)
- decision — docs/decisions/adr-closing-a-room-deletes-its-future-bookings.md
- code — roombooker/core/identity.py (identity is only the Pick your name cookie)

## Notes

- Assumption: Anyone can check in a booking they are not part of, so a passer-by can keep a booking from being freed; accepted for this release (S11).
- Decision: (2026-11-13) Requirements written with Sofia directly, no PRD (the user's call).
- Decision: (2026-11-13) No numeric success target this release (S15).

# Codebase research: booking lifecycle and end

This document describes how bookings end in room-booker at commit `9184f9d`, and what reads or depends on how they end. It is for whoever plans the next change and for anyone checking a single claim. Every claim cites a line or a commit. It recommends nothing.

In short, a booking ends in one of three ways: its end time passes and nothing is written (question 1a); the organiser cancels and Python deletes the row (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`); or the room closes and a trigger deletes its bookings that have not started (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). No column records an end state (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`).

## Questions

1. (how) How does a booking stop being active today? What marks its end (end time, cancellation, deletion, anything else), and which code paths and database triggers produce each one?
2. (what touches) What reads a booking's end time, or depends on a booking existing or being removed? This covers listings, calendar views, the iCal download and feed, overlap checks, room closing, and seed/demo data.
3. (how) How do the overlap triggers (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`) and the trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` decide which bookings count, for example past or future, and current or removed?
4. (why) Why is the end of a booking represented the way it is, for example as a delete rather than a recorded state?
5. (how) How are a booking's lifecycle, its end, and its removal tested?

Researchers ran as fresh subagents given only these questions. They were Claude Code subagent types, which may load the repository's `AGENTS.md`; nothing in that file names the work in progress.

## 1. How a booking stops being active

A booking has no status, cancelled, or soft-delete column. It is a row with `id`, `room_id`, `organiser_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at`, the times stored as UTC text (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`). The schema adds `CheckConstraint("end_at > start_at")` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). A booking stops being active in one of three ways. Deactivating a person is not one of them.

**1a. Its end time passes. Nothing is written.** "Ended" is computed at read time by comparing `end_at` with `core.time.utc_now()`:

- The upcoming list filters on `end_at > after`, with `after = utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`).
- The details page sets `has_ended = booking.end_at <= uk.utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/web.py:257 (booking_details) @ 9184f9d`). The template hides Cancel unless `booking.can_cancel and not has_ended` (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:34 (content) @ 9184f9d`).
- The service refuses to cancel once `end_at <= utc_now()` and raises `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; the message is at `roombooker/bookings/service.py:46 (ALREADY_ENDED) @ 9184f9d`).

# Codebase research: booking lifecycle and end

This document describes how bookings end in room-booker at commit `9184f9d`, and what reads or depends on how they end. It is for whoever plans the next change and for anyone checking a single claim. Every claim cites a line or a commit. It recommends nothing.

In short, a booking ends in one of three ways: its end time passes and nothing is written (question 1a); the organiser cancels and Python deletes the row (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:364-371 (cancel) @ 9184f9d`); or the room closes and a trigger deletes its bookings that have not started (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:84-95 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). No column records an end state (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`).

## Questions

1. (how) How does a booking stop being active today? What marks its end (end time, cancellation, deletion, anything else), and which code paths and database triggers produce each one?
2. (what touches) What reads a booking's end time, or depends on a booking existing or being removed? This covers listings, calendar views, the iCal download and feed, overlap checks, room closing, and seed/demo data.
3. (how) How do the overlap triggers (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py`) and the trigger `rooms_close_cancels_future_bookings` decide which bookings count, for example past or future, and current or removed?
4. (why) Why is the end of a booking represented the way it is, for example as a delete rather than a recorded state?
5. (how) How are a booking's lifecycle, its end, and its removal tested?

Researchers ran as fresh subagents given only these questions. They were Claude Code subagent types, which may load the repository's `AGENTS.md`; nothing in that file names the work in progress.

## 1. How a booking stops being active

A booking has no status, cancelled, or soft-delete column. It is a row with `id`, `room_id`, `organiser_id`, `title`, `start_at` and `end_at`, the times stored as UTC text (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:16-25 (bookings) @ 9184f9d`). The schema adds `CheckConstraint("end_at > start_at")` (`migrations/versions/0003_bookings.py:54-56 (upgrade) @ 9184f9d`). A booking stops being active in one of three ways. Deactivating a person is not one of them.

**1a. Its end time passes. Nothing is written.** "Ended" is computed at read time by comparing `end_at` with `core.time.utc_now()`:

- The upcoming list filters on `end_at > after`, with `after = utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/store.py:54-63 (upcoming_for_organiser) @ 9184f9d`, `roombooker/bookings/service.py:200-205 (upcoming_bookings) @ 9184f9d`).
- The details page sets `has_ended = booking.end_at <= uk.utc_now()` (`roombooker/bookings/web.py:257 (booking_details) @ 9184f9d`). The template hides Cancel unless `booking.can_cancel and not has_ended` (`roombooker/templates/bookings/details.html:34 (content) @ 9184f9d`).
- The service refuses to cancel once `end_at <= utc_now()` and raises `InvalidBooking(ALREADY_ENDED)` (`roombooker/bookings/service.py:359-360 (booking_to_cancel) @ 9184f9d`; the message is at `roombooker/bookings/service.py:46 (ALREADY_ENDED) @ 9184f9d`).

# BMad UX

## Overview

You are a master UX facilitator. **Elicit and capture** the user's vision, never impose yours. Probe like a senior practitioner; never volunteer colors, patterns, or directions unless a theme is already in place and the user confirms it. Render options via creative tools when seeing helps; the picks are the user's.

Produce two peer contracts: **`DESIGN.md`** (visual identity per the [Google Labs spec](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md) — owns *how it looks*) and **`EXPERIENCE.md`** (information architecture, behavior, states, interactions, accessibility, journeys — owns *how it works*). EXPERIENCE.md cross-references DESIGN.md tokens by name using `{path.to.token}` syntax. Both spines win on conflict with any mock, wireframe, or import.

## The DESIGN.md spine

Per the [Google Labs spec](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md). YAML frontmatter tokens (**colors** · **typography** · **rounded** · **spacing** · **components**) + markdown body in canonical order: **Brand & Style** · **Colors** · **Typography** · **Layout & Spacing** · **Elevation & Depth** · **Shapes** · **Components** · **Do's and Don'ts**. Sections omittable; order locked when present. Spec rules: `references/design-md-spec.md`. Shape: read every entry in `{workflow.design_md_examples}`.

## The EXPERIENCE.md spine

Always: **Foundation** (form-factor, UI system when present; DESIGN.md is the visual identity reference) · **Information Architecture** · **Voice and Tone** (microcopy — brand voice lives in DESIGN.md.Brand & Style) · **Component Patterns** (behavioral — visual specs live in DESIGN.md.Components) · **State Patterns** · **Interaction Primitives** · **Accessibility Floor** (behavioral — visual contrast lives in DESIGN.md) · **Key Flows** (named-protagonist journeys with a climax beat).

When triggered: **Inspiration & Anti-patterns** · **Responsive & Platform**.

Invent sections for product-specific concerns. Shape: read every entry in `{workflow.experience_md_examples}`.

When Foundation names a UI system (shadcn, MUI, native UIKit, Compose, internal design system), both spines inherit from it; DESIGN.md tokens reference or extend the system's defaults, EXPERIENCE.md specifies only the behavioral delta.

## Sources

When a ticket exists for the work, read it first and in full and work from its Requirements; open its `sources:` and `companions:` only for a need the ticket points at. With no ticket, UX may lead or stand alone. DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md hold design and experience decisions, not duplicates of upstream product content.

## On Activation

1. Resolve customization: `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --project-root {project-root} --key workflow`.

Outcomes, in order:

- **Spines distilled.** Subagent reads `.memlog.md`, `.working/`, `imports/`, and the ticket in full, opening a source only where the memlog or ticket cites it; produces `DESIGN.md` against `## The DESIGN.md spine` + `{workflow.design_md_examples}` and `EXPERIENCE.md` against `## The EXPERIENCE.md spine` + `{workflow.experience_md_examples}`. Runs the rubric walker's Pass 1 coverage checks proactively (see `references/validate.md`). Surface gaps; never invent.
- **Inputs reconciled.** Subagent per user-supplied input → `reconcile-{input}.md`. Surface dropped qualitative ideas.
- **Reviewer Gate offered.** Ask whether to run validation; if yes, present the lens menu (see `## Reviewer Gate`) and let the user pick. If any lens ran, resolve findings before polish; otherwise proceed.
- **Open items triaged.** Open Questions, `[ASSUMPTION]`, `[NOTE FOR UX]`. Phase-blockers one at a time; non-blockers → `memlog.py append`.
- **Key-screen mocks rendered.** Key-screens tool → `.working/` for surfaces where layout drives behavior or anchors visual language.
- **Mock coverage confirmed.** Walk every IA surface; classify *mocked* vs *spine-only*. Ask: *"These will be built from spine tables alone — any need a visual reference?"* Render more if named; log spine-only choices.
- **Layout extracted, artifacts promoted.** Distill subagent re-reads each `.working/` and `imports/` artifact; lifts visual decisions into DESIGN.md and behavioral decisions into EXPERIENCE.md. Promote `.working/` keepers to `mockups/` (HTML) or `wireframes/` (Excalidraw); imports stay. Inline relative links at relevant spine sections; state spines-win-on-conflict once.
- **Polished, handed off, closed.** Apply `{workflow.doc_standards}` in order. Execute `{workflow.external_handoffs}`; surface URLs. Set both files' `status: final`, `updated: {date}`. Log finalization via `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/memlog.py append --workspace {doc_workspace} --type event --text "spines finalized"`. Share paths. Common next: `bmad-architecture`, asking Sofia (`bmad-agent-po`) to update the ticket's requirements from the spines, `bmad-build`. Run `{workflow.on_complete}`.

# Check-in request, 2026-11-13

The request as Ilya gave it to BMad on 2026-11-13, word for word:

> Start a new initiative called check-in. People check in at a tablet by the room's door, and rooms nobody checks into are freed. I want requirements, UX, architecture, stories and build.

- S1: People check in at a tablet by the room's door.
- S2: Rooms nobody checks into are freed.

Answers given while writing the initiative's requirements are added below, each with its own S-number.

## Answers to Sofia, 2026-11-13, word for word

> This is a new feature for our existing room booking app. Read the deep-recon account of how bookings end today.
>
> Booked rooms often sit empty because nobody turns up.
>
> Each room gets a tablet by its door, showing the room's bookings for today. People check in on the tablet, from 5 minutes before the start until 15 minutes after.
>
> If nobody checks in within 15 minutes of the start, the room is freed: anyone can book the rest of that slot, and the booking shows as freed in its owner's calendar.
>
> Office managers see how many bookings were freed in their office this week.
>
> No QR codes, sensors, badges or notifications in this release. The tablets are ordinary tablets showing a web page, and an office manager sets each one up once.

- S3: The problem: booked rooms often sit empty because nobody turns up.
- S4: Each room gets a tablet by its door showing the room's bookings for today.
- S5: People check in on the tablet from 5 minutes before the start until 15 minutes after.
- S6: If nobody checks in within 15 minutes of the start, the room is freed: anyone can book the rest of that slot, and the booking shows as freed in its owner's calendar.
- S7: Office managers see how many bookings were freed in their office this week.
- S8: Out of this release: QR codes, sensors, badges, notifications.
- S9: The tablets are ordinary tablets showing a web page; an office manager sets each one up once.
- S10: It is a new feature of the existing room booking app; the deep-recon account of how bookings end today (`_bmad-output/research-booking-lifecycle-and-end/research-booking-lifecycle-and-end.md`) is an input.

## Sofia's proposals, accepted 2026-11-13

- S11: (Sofia's proposal, accepted with "All fine.") Anyone at the tablet checks in a booking with one tap, without saying who they are.
- S12: (Sofia's proposal, accepted.) A freed booking shows as "Freed: nobody checked in" on My bookings and the booking's details page, and as cancelled in the organiser's subscribed calendar.
- S13: (Sofia's proposal, accepted.) Rooms whose tablet has not been set up are never freed.
- S14: (Sofia's proposal, accepted.) "This week" for the freed count is Monday to today, UK time, shown to office managers beside their office's rooms on Manage rooms.
- S15: (Sofia's proposal, accepted.) No numeric success target this release: the signal is that unclaimed bookings are freed and managers can see the count.

# DESIGN.md Spec — Working Reference

Source of truth: [google-labs-code/design.md](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md) (Apache 2.0, Google Labs, April 2026). This file is a working summary; the URL wins on conflict.

## Structure

YAML frontmatter (machine-readable tokens) + markdown body (human-readable rationale, prose sections).

## Frontmatter tokens

| Key | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Required. Brand or system name. |
| `description` | string | One-line statement of what this system is. |
| `colors` | flat object | Kebab-case keys. Values are hex strings (`'#FBF9F4'`). |
| `typography` | nested object | Each value: an object with any subset of `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`. |
| `rounded` | object | Scale names (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `full`, `DEFAULT`) → CSS dimensions. `full` is conventionally `9999px`. |
| `spacing` | object | Scale levels (`'1'`, `'2'`, ...) or named tokens (`gutter`, `margin-mobile`, `editorial-gap`) → dimensions. |
| `components` | object | Component-name → object of component tokens mapped to values or `{path.to.token}` references. |

## Body sections (omittable, order-locked when present)

1. **Brand & Style** — Aesthetic posture in prose. The editorial voice — what *kind* of thing this is.
2. **Colors** — Per-color story. Why each exists, where it's used, what it's *not* used for.
3. **Typography** — Type roles, ramp, and rules. Platform conventions noted semantically when inherited.
4. **Layout & Spacing** — Spacing scale narrative, grid behavior, margins, gutters, breakpoint rules.
5. **Elevation & Depth** — Shadow language and tonal layering rules.
6. **Shapes** — Corner radii rules and the aesthetic logic behind them.
7. **Components** — Per-component visual specs: anatomy, color usage, sizing, state appearance.
8. **Do's and Don'ts** — Hard visual rules — what to do, what to avoid.

Sections may be omitted when not relevant; order is locked when present.

## Cross-reference syntax

`{path.to.token}` used in prose and inside component objects to reference frontmatter tokens. Examples:

- `{colors.primary}`
- `{typography.body.fontSize}`
- `{rounded.md}`
- `{spacing.4}`

The path follows the YAML structure.

## Common patterns

- **Light/dark mode.** Either separate kebab-case tokens (`surface-base` / `surface-base-dark`) or separate DESIGN.md files per mode. The spec allows either; pick the form that reads cleanest for the product.
- **Platform conventions.** When inheriting from native platforms (iOS UIKit, Android Compose, Apple Human Interface Guidelines), use a `note` field instead of literal values: `{ note: 'iOS Title 1 · Android Headline Small' }`. The spec is the spec; the platform owns the rendered values.
- **UI-system inheritance.** When inheriting from shadcn / MUI / Tailwind / internal design system, reference the system's tokens by name rather than restating values. DESIGN.md specifies only the deltas (brand color overrides, typography swaps, component customizations).
- **Component tokens.** The `components` frontmatter entry maps each named component (e.g., `button-primary`) to its specific token values. Use `{path.to.token}` references freely; the resolver flattens at consumption time.

50	
51	## Brand & Style
52	
53	Drift is a focused task tracker for solo founders and small async teams. The product premise is that *work is a moving thing* — momentum matters more than perfectly groomed backlogs, and the right tool surfaces what you're working on *now* without making you administer a system to find it. The brand expression follows: a serif display moment in an otherwise sober sans-serif surface, a single warm accent that means *this is what's live*, and visual restraint everywhere else.
54	
55	Drift inherits shadcn/ui defaults wholesale. This DESIGN.md specifies only the brand-layer deltas — primary color, accent color, display typography, slightly tighter corners, and a handful of brand-specific components. The 80% of components that ship from shadcn (Button, Card, Dialog, Sheet, Command, Popover, Toast) inherit shadcn's visual specs as-is. Customizing those is *explicitly* against the brand discipline — shadcn's defaults are the contract.
56	
57	## Colors
58	
59	The Drift palette is two colors of brand-layer plus shadcn defaults for everything else.
60	
61	- **Primary Navy (`#0F4C81` light / `#5C8AC2` dark)** is the brand color. Used on primary buttons, active nav items, link underlines, and the "current week" indicator. Replaces shadcn's default `primary`.
62	- **Focus Amber (`#F59E0B` light / `#FBC470` dark)** is the accent. Used exclusively to indicate the task or project currently in focus — the one you're working on *right now*. Never used for chrome, never used decoratively, never used for state badges. Amber means "live."
63	- **All other tokens** (`background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `border`, `input`, `ring`, `card`, `popover`, `destructive`) inherit from shadcn defaults. If the brand can't justify overriding a token, it doesn't override it.
64	
65	Avoid: chromatic flourishes, gradient surfaces, custom destructive colors (use shadcn's), more than two brand colors. The discipline is two-colors-and-stop.
66	
67	## Typography
68	
69	Body / label / caption inherit shadcn's Geist Sans ramp. Only the `display` role is brand-overridden, set in **Instrument Serif** at 36px (24px small variant). The serif moment appears in:
70	
71	- Empty-state hero text on Today and project surfaces
72	- Project titles in the project detail header
73	- The "Welcome back, {name}" greeting at first session of the day
74	
75	Everything else stays in Geist Sans. The serif is a punctuation mark, not a default voice.
76	
77	## Layout & Spacing
78	
79	shadcn / Tailwind spacing scale inherited as-is (the 4-based scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64). Maximum content width: `max-w-3xl` (768px) — Drift is not a wide-table product, and forcing one-column reading keeps the surface focused.
80	
81	Single-column layout. Sidebar nav on `lg` (1024px+); on smaller viewports, the sidebar becomes a sheet triggered from the top bar.
82	
83	## Elevation & Depth
84	
85	Inherited from shadcn — subtle shadow on hover/active states, no elevation as a visual hierarchy device. Drift adds nothing on top of this; brand discipline is "shadcn's shadows are correct."
86	
87	## Shapes
88	
89	Tighter than shadcn defaults: `rounded/sm` (4px) for inputs, `rounded/md` (6px) for cards and buttons, `rounded/lg` (8px) for dialogs and the command palette. The crispness reads "tool" rather than "consumer app." Pill shapes (`rounded/full`) appear only on status badges.
90	
91	## Components
92	
93	Drift uses the following shadcn components as-is, unchanged: `Button`, `Card`, `Dialog`, `Sheet`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`, `Toast`, `Tabs`, `Avatar`, `Separator`. The contract: don't customize these.
94	
95	Brand-layer-overridden components:
96	
97	- **Button (primary variant)** — `{colors.primary}` fill, `{colors.primary-foreground}` text, `{rounded.md}` corner. Other variants (secondary, outline, ghost, destructive) inherit shadcn defaults.
98	- **Focus card** — Custom Drift component. The "this is what you're working on now" card on Today and project detail. `{colors.accent}` fill, no border, slightly elevated. Appears at most once per surface.
99	- **Command palette result (active)** — Override on shadcn's `Command` component: the highlighted/keyboard-selected result row uses `{colors.accent}` instead of shadcn's default `accent` token. Reinforces "this is what will fire if you hit Enter."
100	
101	## Do's and Don'ts
102	
103	| Do | Don't |
104	|---|---|
105	| Inherit shadcn defaults for everything not in the brand layer | Override shadcn's color tokens beyond `primary` and `accent` |
106	| Use `{colors.accent}` only for "live / now / in-focus" | Use accent for state, chrome, or hover affordances |
107	| `display` typography sparingly — empty states, hero greetings | Set body text in `display` to "make it pretty" |
108	| Tighter corners than shadcn (4 / 6 / 8) | Use shadcn's default 6/8/12 (Drift reads sharper) |
109	| Single-column layouts inside `max-w-3xl` | Wide multi-column tables (Drift is not a spreadsheet) |

9	# Drift — Experience Spine
10	
11	> Illustrative example. Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js + Tailwind. Paired with `design-example-shadcn.md` (Drift DESIGN.md). Demonstrates: component-library inheritance, keyboard-first interaction primitives, the "shadcn + brand-layer" pattern that covers most modern web SaaS.
12	
13	## Foundation
14	
15	Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js 15+ with Tailwind CSS. The component library does most of the work; brand discipline is "respect the defaults except where the brand layer overrides them." `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference and names the override surface; this spine is the experience. Single-tenant per project; users can belong to multiple projects but each project is a self-contained workspace.
16	
17	## Information Architecture
18	
19	| Surface | Reached from | Purpose |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| Today | App open / `g t` | Current focus, in-progress tasks pulled from all projects |
22	| Projects | Sidebar / `g p` | List of active and archived projects |
23	| Project detail | Projects row / `g 1`–`g 9` | Tasks in this project, organized by lane |
24	| Search | `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` | Command palette — surface, navigate, act |
25	| Settings | Avatar menu | Account, theme, keyboard shortcuts, billing |
26

# Drift — Experience Spine

> Illustrative example. Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js + Tailwind. Paired with `design-example-shadcn.md` (Drift DESIGN.md). Demonstrates: component-library inheritance, keyboard-first interaction primitives, the "shadcn + brand-layer" pattern that covers most modern web SaaS.

## Foundation

Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js 15+ with Tailwind CSS. The component library does most of the work; brand discipline is "respect the defaults except where the brand layer overrides them." `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference and names the override surface; this spine is the experience. Single-tenant per project; users can belong to multiple projects but each project is a self-contained workspace.

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Today | App open / `g t` | Current focus, in-progress tasks pulled from all projects |
| Projects | Sidebar / `g p` | List of active and archived projects |
| Project detail | Projects row / `g 1`–`g 9` | Tasks in this project, organized by lane |
| Search | `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` | Command palette — surface, navigate, act |
| Settings | Avatar menu | Account, theme, keyboard shortcuts, billing |

Sidebar collapses to icons on `md`; becomes a `Sheet` on `sm`. Modal stacks one level deep (e.g., open `Dialog` on top of a surface, never on top of another dialog).

→ Composition reference: `mockups/today.html`, `mockups/project-detail.html`, `mockups/command-palette.html`. Spine wins on conflict.

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy. Brand voice and aesthetic posture live in `DESIGN.md`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "What are you working on?" | "Let's get productive! 🚀" |
| "3 tasks in motion" | "You have 3 active items." |
| "Closed. Nice work." | "Task completed successfully ✓" |
| "Nothing in motion. Pick something." | "No active tasks. Click below to get started!" |
| Manager-facing: counts and verbs. Employee-facing: same. | Different tone per audience — Drift talks to everyone the same way. |

## Component Patterns

Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components` (or in shadcn defaults, when inherited).

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Task row | Projects, Today | Click anywhere on row opens edit dialog. Checkbox toggles done state with optimistic update. Hover reveals quick-actions (`focus`, `defer`, `archive`). |
| Focus card | Today, Project detail | At most one focus card per surface — the task or project marked with `focus` state. `f` keyboard shortcut sets focus on the active row. |
| Command palette | Global (⌘K) | Fuzzy search across all projects, tasks, and commands. `Enter` fires the highlighted result. `→` previews a result. Escape closes. |
| Project header | Project detail | Inline-editable title (click to edit, blur to save). Status pill: active / archived / done. |
| Empty state | Anywhere | shadcn's empty pattern + one Drift-specific sentence. `display-sm` for the headline, body text below, single primary action. |

## State Patterns

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Cold app load | Today | shadcn `Skeleton` rows (4-6) match expected layout. Resolves on data. |
| No focus | Today | `display-sm`: "Nothing in motion. Pick something." Below: list of in-progress tasks from all projects. |
| Empty project | Project detail | `display-sm`: "{Project title} is empty." Body: "Add a first task to get going." Single primary button. |
| Command palette no matches | ⌘K | "No matches. Start typing a task or project name, or pick an action below." Followed by 4-5 common commands. |
| Offline | Global (status bar) | shadcn `Toast` once: "You're offline. Changes will sync when you reconnect." Local writes continue. |
| Permission denied | Projects (others' private) | Surface hidden from sidebar. No "blocked" screen. |
| Stale data | Project detail | If background refresh detects changes, shadcn `Toast`: "Updated by {collaborator_name}. Refresh." Manual refresh, no auto. |

## Interaction Primitives

**Keyboard-first.** Drift's primary audience is developers and power users; the keyboard surface is the product, the mouse is fallback.

- `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` — Command palette (universal)
- `g t` / `g p` — Go to Today / Projects (vim-style)
- `g 1`–`g 9` — Go to project by sidebar position
- `f` — Set focus on highlighted task/project
- `c` — Create new task (context-aware: in the active project)
- `Esc` — Close dialogs, exit edit mode, clear command palette
- `/` — Focus search in current surface

**Mouse:** click to act, drag deferred to v2. Hover reveals row actions on `md+` (touch users tap to reveal).

**Banned everywhere:** infinite scroll (pagination only), drag-to-reorder in v1, hover-only affordances on `sm` viewports, modal stacks > 1 level deep.

## Accessibility Floor

Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (inherits shadcn's WCAG AA-compliant defaults; brand overrides verified to maintain ratios).

- WCAG 2.2 AA across the responsive web surface.
- Screen reader announces page surface on navigation: "Today, focus surface" / "Project: {name}, task list, {N} tasks."
- Keyboard shortcuts available without modifier on most surfaces (vim-style `g t` etc.) — users with motor-control limitations get the same surface as power users.
- `Tab` order matches reading order on every surface. `Esc` always closes the topmost modal/popover.
- Command palette is fully keyboard-operable; results announce as they update via `aria-live`.
- Focus rings inherit shadcn's `ring` token — visible at AA contrast against `background`.

## Responsive & Platform

| Breakpoint | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `≥ lg` (1024px+) | Sidebar visible. Today is a 2-column layout: focus + in-motion list. |
| `md` (768–1023px) | Sidebar collapses to icons. Today stacks to single column. |
| `< md` (`sm`) | Sidebar becomes a `Sheet` triggered from top bar. Command palette opens fullscreen. |

Drift is responsive web, not a native mobile app. The product works on phones for read + simple-edit, but the primary surface is desktop / laptop.

## Inspiration & Anti-patterns

- **Lifted from Linear:** the keyboard-first discipline. `⌘K` is the command center; vim-style nav (`g t`); no drag for primary navigation; status pill vocabulary.
- **Lifted from Notion:** inline-editable titles. Click-to-edit on project header, blur to save. No edit/view mode toggle.
- **Lifted from shadcn:** the entire surface vocabulary. Drift's brand is *what we add to shadcn*, not a from-scratch design system. This is a deliberate posture, not a shortcut.
- **Rejected — Streaks, badges, achievement notifications:** Drift is a tool, not a habit app. Task closure is its own reward; no celebratory animation, no "🎉 5-day streak!" toast.
- **Rejected — AI-suggested next tasks:** Drift surfaces what's in motion, doesn't tell the user what to work on. The user picks focus; the tool surfaces consequences.
- **Rejected — Multi-column kanban as default project view:** lists are linear; kanban hides progress behind columns. Optional v2; not the default.

## Key Flows

### Flow 1 — Morning focus (Sarah, solo founder, 8:45am Tuesday)

1. Sarah opens Drift in a browser tab.
2. App loads Today. `display-sm`: "Welcome back, Sarah." Focus card shows yesterday's marked task — "Finish landing page hero copy" — still in motion.
3. She hits `⌘K`, types "ship hero", sees the matching task and presses Enter to open it.
4. Inline edit: she updates the task description with two new bullets. Tab + Tab triggers save.
5. **Climax:** Sarah closes the dialog. Today re-renders: focus card still shows the hero task, but now with the updated body text visible at a glance. She doesn't have to navigate anywhere — the surface that greeted her now reflects the work she just did. She picks up her coffee and starts writing.

Failure: data save fails → shadcn `Toast` (destructive variant): "Couldn't save. Trying again." Inline edit retained; another `Enter` retries.

### Flow 2 — Async handoff (Devon and Mara, small remote team, mid-afternoon)

1. Devon finishes wiring up the auth flow and marks the task `done`.
2. Mara, time-zoned three hours ahead and online during overlap, opens Drift.
3. Today loads; her focus is on her own front-end work, but the in-motion list shows Devon's auth task now marked done and one task below it newly assigned to her — "Wire up post-auth redirect" — that Devon set during checkout.
4. She hits `f` on the row to mark it as her focus, then `Enter` to open it.
5. **Climax:** The focus card swaps. Her surface now shows the post-auth redirect task as the live thing she's working on; the projects sidebar shows the Auth project highlighted; the command palette `⌘K` defaults its first result to "Go to Auth project." The state of the team's progress is *embedded in her surface* — no Slack thread to scroll, no status doc to read.

Failure: Devon hadn't actually assigned the follow-up — Mara mis-assigned to herself. She hits `Esc`, `f` again to unfocus, and reassigns to Devon. No "are you sure" dialog; Drift trusts the user.

## Brand & Style

The door screen is the existing Room Booking app seen from across a corridor. It keeps the app's plain, quiet, navy-and-white look. It adds no new colours, no new typeface and no decoration. The only change is scale. The room name, the word "Free" or "Booked", and the current booking are big enough to read from a few steps away. Everything else on the screen is secondary and can stay small.

The check-in states in My bookings follow the same rule. Each state is a word on the booking, not a new visual language.

## Colors

All colours are inherited from `roombooker/static/tokens.css`. The door screen adds none.

- **Navy (`{colors.navy}`)** fills the status panel when the room is booked. A navy panel or a white one is the cue you can read from furthest away, before any word is legible. Navy keeps its existing meaning: a booking.
- **White (`{colors.white}`)** with a navy border is the status panel when the room is free. It matches the app's existing free slot (`--slot-free-*`).
- **Closed grey (`{colors.closed}`)** is the panel for a closed room and the fill for a freed booking in My bookings. The app already uses grey for out of use, not an error (`app.css`: "grey, never red"). A freed booking is the same kind of thing.

## Typography

Body, label, meta and title are inherited from `tokens.css`. The door screen adds one ramp of five sizes, all in the app's system-ui stack. `[ASSUMPTION]` These values assume a roughly 10-inch tablet at its default zoom. Check them on the real device from 2–3 m before building.

| Role | Token | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Status | `{typography.door-status}` | "Free", "Booked", "Closed". The largest text on screen. |
| Room | `{typography.door-room}` | The room name, above the status. |
| Current | `{typography.door-current}` | The current or next booking's title, and the Check in label. |
| Detail | `{typography.door-detail}` | Times and the check-in countdown ("Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in"). |
| List | `{typography.door-list}` | Rows in today's list. Read close up. |

My bookings uses the existing ramp. The state tag uses `{typography.label}`.

## Layout & Spacing

The door screen fills the viewport, with no top bar, no tabs, no person and no scroll at the default zoom. `[ASSUMPTION]` The tablet is in landscape.

- **Landscape:** the status panel takes the left ~60%. It holds the room name, status, current booking and the Check in button. Today's list takes the right ~40%. The outer gutter is `{spacing.door-gutter}`.
- **Portrait:** the status panel is on top, with today's list below it. A long list scrolls inside its own column. The status panel never scrolls off the screen.

My bookings keeps its existing layout and gains only a tag line on each booking.

## Elevation & Depth

None, as in the rest of the app. Panels are flat fills with borders.

## Shapes

Inherited: `{rounded.md}` for panels and the Check in button, `{rounded.sm}` for list rows and tags.

## Components

- **Door status panel.** Three variants: `door-status-panel-booked` (navy fill, white text), `door-status-panel-free` (white fill, navy border and text) and `door-status-panel-closed` (grey). Anatomy, top to bottom:
  1. room name in `door-room`
  2. status word in `door-status`
  3. current booking title in `door-current`, with its times in `door-detail`
  4. the countdown line in `door-detail`, when check-in is open
  5. the Check in button

  When the room is free, line 3 becomes "Next: {title} at 14:00" or "Nothing else today".
- **Door Check in button.** Full width of the status panel and `{spacing.door-check-in-height}` tall, more than twice the app's touch target. On the navy panel it is a white button with navy text. That is the app's secondary button inverted, so it stands out on navy without a new colour. The label is "Check in" in `door-current`. While pressed it shows `{colors.navy-tint}`.
- **Checked-in confirmation.** The button is replaced by the line "✓ Checked in" in `door-current`, white on the navy panel. No button remains.
- **Door list item.** One row per booking today: times, then title, then a state word on the right. Variants: current or next booking uses `door-list-item-current` (navy tint), past bookings use `door-list-item-past` (muted ink), the rest use `door-list-item`.
- **Booking state tag (My bookings, details page).** A small label on a booking: "Check in at the door by 10:15", "Checked in" or "Freed: nobody checked in". On the navy organiser link it is white text with no fill. On a freed booking it is muted ink.
- **Freed booking in My bookings.** `calendar-booking-freed`: grey fill with a border and muted ink, so it reads as no longer happening without looking deleted or like an error. The title stays legible and is not struck through.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use navy for booked and white for free, so the screen can be read before any word can | Add green, amber or red for room states |
| Use grey for freed: out of use, not a mistake | Use error red for a freed booking or for "not checked in yet" |
| Keep the room name, status and current booking in the door ramp | Put the list or footer text in the door ramp |
| Use one big Check in button | Add a second action, a confirm step or a who-are-you field next to it |
| Show the status word as well as the panel colour | Let colour alone tell free from booked |

+- **Checked-in confirmation.** The button is replaced by the line "✓ Checked in" in `door-current`, white on the navy panel. No button remains.

+| Use navy for booked and white for free, so the screen can be read before any word can | Add green, amber or red for room states |
+| Use grey for freed: out of use, not a mistake | Use error red for a freed booking or for "not checked in yet" |
+| Keep the room name, status and current booking in the door ramp | Put the list or footer text in the door ramp |
+| Use one big Check in button | Add a second action, a confirm step or a who-are-you field next to it |
+| Show the status word as well as the panel colour | Let colour alone tell free from booked |

---
name: Room Booking — door screen and check-in states
status: draft
ticket: ../initiative-check-in.md
created: 2026-11-13
updated: 2026-11-13
---

# Door screen and check-in states: experience spine

Covers the door tablet's check-in screen (R2, R3, R7), and the check-in and freed states of a booking in My bookings and on its details page (R5). The office manager's tablet setup (R1) and the weekly freed count on Manage rooms (R6) are **not designed here**: the user scoped this run to the two surfaces above. Requirement ids are the initiative's (`../initiative-check-in.md`).

## Foundation

- **Surfaces:** (1) the door screen, a web page of the app shown full screen on an ordinary tablet by each room's door (C2); (2) My bookings and the booking details page, existing pages of the app, gaining check-in states.
- **UI system:** the app's own server-rendered Jinja templates and htmx, with tokens from `roombooker/static/tokens.css`. `DESIGN.md` is the visual reference and names the deltas. Every page works as a full page load, and htmx only narrows the swap with `hx-select` (C5).
- **Who is at the door screen:** anyone walking up. There is no sign-in, no person and no Pick your name. Check-in is anonymous (S11).
- `[ASSUMPTION]` The tablet is roughly 10 inches, in landscape, mounted by the door at standing eye height, and kept awake by its own settings (kiosk mode or never sleep). The app doesn't control the device (C2).

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Door screen | The tablet opens it once set up, and stays on it | Shows the room name, free or booked, the current or next booking, and today's list. Offers one-tap check-in while the window is open. | R2, R3, R7 |
| My bookings (Day, Week) | Top bar tab, as today | Each booking in a room with a tablet carries its check-in state | R5 |
| Booking details | A booking in My bookings or Rooms, as today | Shows the booking's check-in state and hides actions that no longer apply | R5 |

The door screen has no links out: no top bar, no tabs, no "Back". `[ASSUMPTION]` Its only control is Check in, so passers-by can't wander off it into the app.

Not designed here, and needed before the initiative is done: the setup surface (R1), the freed count (R6), and whether a freed booking still appears in the Rooms page's booking list (`bookings/_item.html`).

## Voice and Tone

Plain UK English, 24-hour clock, en dash in time ranges ("10:00–11:00"), and no exclamation marks, matching the existing "Room becomes free for everyone".

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "Free" / "Booked" / "Closed" | "Available" / "Occupied" / "In use" |
| "Check in" | "Claim room", "I'm here", "Start meeting" |
| "Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in" | "Check in now or lose your room!" |
| "✓ Checked in" | "Check-in successful" |
| "Freed: nobody checked in" (exact, R5) | "No-show", "Released", "Auto-cancelled" |
| "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15" | "Remember to check in!" |
| "Couldn't check in. Tap Check in again." | "Error 500" |
| "Check-in closed at 10:15" | "Too late" |

## Component Patterns

Behavioural rules. Visual specs are in `DESIGN.md` Components.

| Component | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Door status panel | Shows the room's state now: **Booked** when a booking is current (started, not ended, not freed), or when the next booking's check-in window has opened. **Free** otherwise. **Closed** when the room is closed. Under the status: the booking it refers to, as title and times. When free: "Next: {title} at 14:00", or "Nothing else today". |
| Check-in countdown | Shown only while a booking's window is open and nobody has checked in: "Freed at {start+15} if nobody checks in". Before the start it reads "Check in from now · Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in". It is a fixed time, not a ticking timer. |
| Check in button | Present only while a booking's window is open (start − 5 min to start + 15 min) and nobody has checked in. One tap posts a plain HTML form and the page comes back with the panel showing "✓ Checked in". No confirm, no name and no undo (S11). `[ASSUMPTION]` No undo: a mistaken check-in only keeps a booking from being freed, which is the accepted trade-off in the initiative's Notes. |
| Check in button: two bookings | Back to back, if the next booking's window opens while the current booking is still running, the panel stays on the current booking and the button names the one it checks in: "Check in: {next title}, 11:00". It never silently targets a different booking from the one the panel shows. |
| Today's list | Every booking today in this room, in time order: times, title, then a state word: "Checked in", "Freed", "Ended" or nothing for upcoming. Current or next is highlighted. Read close up. Rows aren't tappable. |
| Booking state tag (My bookings, details) | Appears only on bookings in a room with a tablet set up (R7): rooms without one show exactly what they show today. Values: "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15" for a booking today that hasn't been checked in and whose window hasn't closed; "Checked in"; "Freed: nobody checked in". |
| Details page, freed booking | A "Check-in" row in the details list reads "Freed: nobody checked in. {Room} was freed at 10:15." Cancel booking is hidden. Book again stays. `[ASSUMPTION]` Add to calendar is hidden, since the booking is no longer happening. |
| Details page, checked-in booking | The "Check-in" row reads "Checked in at the door". `[ASSUMPTION]` No time, since nothing else in the app shows when someone acted. |

## State Patterns

Door screen. "Window" means start − 5 min to start + 15 min.

| State | Panel | Below the status | Button |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free, more bookings later | Free (white) | "Next: Design review at 14:00" | none |
| Free, nothing else today | Free | "Nothing else today" | none |
| Next booking's window open, not yet started | Booked (navy) | Title, "10:00–11:00", countdown | Check in |
| Current, window open, not checked in | Booked | Title, times, countdown | Check in |
| Current, checked in | Booked | Title, times, "✓ Checked in" | none |
| Current, window closed without check-in, room has tablet | Freed: Free (white) | "Freed: nobody checked in", "Free until {next booking start}" or "Free for the rest of today" | none |
| Freed slot rebooked by someone else | Booked | The new booking, by its own rules | by its own window |
| Current booking ended | The next state in this table | | |
| Room closed | Closed (grey) | "Closed" | none |
| Tablet not set up, or its setup removed | Plain page, app look | "This tablet isn't set up for a room. Ask your office manager to set it up." | none |
| Tapped Check in after the window closed (race) | Free, freed | Message: "Check-in closed at 10:15. This booking was freed." | none |
| Tapped Check in when someone already had | Booked | "✓ Checked in". The second tap is treated as success, not an error. | none |
| Check-in failed (server or network) | Unchanged | Error message, error red: "Couldn't check in. Tap Check in again." | Check in, kept |
| Lost connection | Last state stays on screen | `[ASSUMPTION]` After 2 minutes without a successful refresh, a small line: "Not up to date. Checking again…" | as last state |

**Staying current.** The door screen refreshes itself every 30 seconds by an htmx poll that swaps the whole page body with `hx-select`, and by a plain meta refresh as the no-JS fallback (C5). The server decides every state from the time of the request. The screen can lag a boundary by up to 30 s. The server still refuses a check-in after start + 15 (the race row above). `[ASSUMPTION]` 30 s is enough.

My bookings and details:

| State | My bookings link | Details "Check-in" row |
|---|---|---|
| Room has no tablet | unchanged | no row |
| Today, window not yet closed, not checked in | navy link + "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15" | "Check in at the door from 09:55 until 10:15, or the room is freed" |
| Checked in | navy link + "Checked in" | "Checked in at the door" |
| Freed | grey `calendar-booking-freed` + "Freed: nobody checked in" | "Freed: nobody checked in. {Room} was freed at 10:15." |
| Cancelled or removed by room close | gone, as today | n/a |

|---|---|

1. Kingsway has no tablet set up yet. Anna, the office manager, hasn't done it.
2. Bookings in Kingsway show no check-in tag in My bookings and are never freed (R7). Nothing about Kingsway changes from today.

+3. At 14:15 (within 30 s) the panel turns white: **Deansgate / Free**, "Freed: nobody checked in", "Free until 15:00". In today's list the 14:00 row reads "Freed".
+4. At 14:20 Sam walks past looking for somewhere quiet for a call, and reads "Free until 15:00" from the corridor.

Both documents are drafted in `_bmad-output/initiative-check-in/ux-door-screen/`: `DESIGN.md` (how it looks) and `EXPERIENCE.md` (how it works). They're still marked `draft`, because I filled some gaps myself and need you to check them.

**The door screen**
- It's full screen with no top bar and no links out. The room name, "Free"/"Booked" and the current booking use a new set of large sizes made to be read from the door.
- The app's existing colours carry the state: a navy panel means booked, a white panel means free. Grey means closed or freed, as in "out of use", never red. No new colours.
- It has one control, a 96px **Check in** button. It shows only from 5 minutes before the start to 15 minutes after. Tapping it shows "✓ Checked in", with no confirm step and no name.
- When check-in is open, it shows a fixed time, "Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in", rather than a ticking timer.
- Once a booking is freed, the panel turns white and shows "Freed: nobody checked in · Free until 15:00".
- It covers about 14 states, including back-to-back bookings, a tap just after the window closes, two people tapping at once, a lost connection, a closed room and a tablet that isn't set up.

**My bookings and details**
- Rooms with a tablet get a tag on each booking: "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15", "Checked in" or "Freed: nobody checked in".

1. The tablet is about 10 inches, in landscape. The large text sizes (88/48/40px) still need checking on a real device from 2–3 m.
2. Check-in can't be undone.
3. A freed booking hides Add to calendar.
4. **Attendees** see the freed and checked-in states too, not only the organiser. If they didn't, they'd walk to a room that's been given away.
5. The screen refreshes every 30 s, so a state change can show up to 30 s late. The server still refuses a check-in after +15 minutes.
6. Booking titles show on the door screen. Organiser names don't.

**Not designed here, as you scoped it:** tablet setup (R1), the weekly freed count (R6), and whether a freed booking still appears in the Rooms page's list. Something will have to cover these before the initiative is done.

**Before I finish, two choices:**
- **Mocks:** should I render an HTML mock of the door screen (booked with check-in open, checked in, freed) and of a freed booking in My bookings? I'd do the door screen at least, since the layout matters most there.

Answer however suits you, for example "1–6 fine, mock the door screen, no review".
Understood: 1–6 confirmed, no mocks, no review. I'm finalizing now.

+Plain UK English, 24-hour clock, en dash in time ranges ("10:00–11:00"), and no exclamation marks, matching the existing "Room becomes free for everyone".
+
+| Do | Don't |
+|---|---|
+| "Free" / "Booked" / "Closed" | "Available" / "Occupied" / "In use" |
+| "Check in" | "Claim room", "I'm here", "Start meeting" |
+| "Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in" | "Check in now or lose your room!" |
+| "✓ Checked in" | "Check-in successful" |
+| "Freed: nobody checked in" (exact, R5) | "No-show", "Released", "Auto-cancelled" |
+| "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15" | "Remember to check in!" |

+## State Patterns
+
+Door screen. "Window" means start − 5 min to start + 15 min.
+
+| State | Panel | Below the status | Button |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Free, more bookings later | Free (white) | "Next: Design review at 14:00" | none |
+| Free, nothing else today | Free | "Nothing else today" | none |
+| Next booking's window open, not yet started | Booked (navy) | Title, "10:00–11:00", countdown | Check in |
+| Current, window open, not checked in | Booked | Title, times, countdown | Check in |
+| Current, checked in | Booked | Title, times, "✓ Checked in" | none |

+| Room closed | Closed (grey) | "Closed" | none |

+| Check-in failed (server or network) | Unchanged | Error message, error red: "Couldn't check in. Tap Check in again." | Check in, kept |

+My bookings and details:
+
+| State | My bookings link | Details "Check-in" row |
+|---|---|---|
+| Room has no tablet | unchanged | no row |
+| Today, window not yet closed, not checked in | navy link + "Check in at the door, 09:55–10:15" | "Check in at the door from 09:55 until 10:15, or the room is freed" |
+| Checked in | navy link + "Checked in" | "Checked in at the door" |
+| Freed | grey `calendar-booking-freed` + "Freed: nobody checked in" | "Freed: nobody checked in. {Room} was freed at 10:15." |
+| Cancelled or removed by room close | gone, as today | n/a |
+

+
+## Interaction Primitives
+
+- **Door screen: one tap, nothing else.** No typing, no scrolling at the default zoom, no swipes, no long-press, no gestures.

+- Taps are idempotent: a double tap or two people tapping gives one check-in and both see "✓ Checked in".
+- My bookings and details: no new interactions, only new text and the freed fill.
+- **Banned on the door screen:** any confirm dialog, any name or code entry, any link out of the page, booking from the tablet (Boundaries), sound, notifications (C1), QR codes (C1).
+
+## Accessibility Floor
+
+Behavioural. Contrast is in `DESIGN.md` (navy on white and white on navy, both well past AA).
+
+- WCAG 2.2 AA on all three surfaces.
+- Free and booked are always said in words. Colour only reinforces them.
+- The Check in button is at least 96 px tall and spans the panel, reachable from a wheelchair if the tablet is mounted within reach. Setup guidance for office managers should name a mounting height, and belongs with R1.

+- No motion, no flashing, no ticking countdown. The only time limit is the check-in window itself, which is the product rule. It is shown as a clock time, never as a timer that counts down.
+- Door page has `lang="en-GB"` and a `<title>` of "{Room} · Room Booking".
+
+## Responsive & Platform
+
+| Orientation | Behaviour |
+|---|---|
+| Landscape (assumed) | Status panel left ~60%, today's list right ~40%. Nothing scrolls. |
+| Portrait | Status panel on top, list below. The list scrolls inside itself and the panel stays visible. |
+| Phone-sized | Not a target. The page still works, stacked, so anyone opening the door URL in a browser can see it. |
+
+## Key Flows
+
+### Flow 1: Checking in, a few minutes late (Priya, Leeds, Aire, Tuesday 10:07)
+
+1. Priya has booked Aire 10:00–11:00 for "Client review". She's running late from the station, with two colleagues and the client behind her.

+5. Later in My bookings, her 10:00 booking reads "Checked in".

+Failure: the tablet lost Wi-Fi. The tap shows "Couldn't check in. Tap Check in again." She taps again once the connection is back, still before 10:15.
+
+### Flow 2: A room nobody came to is freed (Tom, Sam and Deansgate, Manchester, Thursday)

+

+2. Bookings in Kingsway show no check-in tag in My bookings and are never freed (R7). Nothing about Kingsway changes from today.

## Brand & Style

The door screen is the existing Room Booking app seen from across a corridor. It keeps the app's plain, quiet, navy-and-white look. It adds no new colours, no new typeface and no decoration. The only change is scale. The room name, the word "Free" or "Booked", and the current booking are big enough to read from a few steps away. Everything else on the screen is secondary and can stay small.

The check-in states in My bookings follow the same rule. Each state is a word on the booking, not a new visual language.

## Colors

All colours are inherited from `roombooker/static/tokens.css`. The door screen adds none.

- **Navy (`{colors.navy}`)** fills the status panel when the room is booked. A navy panel or a white one is the cue you can read from furthest away, before any word is legible. Navy keeps its existing meaning: a booking.
- **White (`{colors.white}`)** with a navy border is the status panel when the room is free. It matches the app's existing free slot (`--slot-free-*`).
- **Closed grey (`{colors.closed}`)** is the panel for a closed room and the fill for a freed booking in My bookings. The app already uses grey for out of use, not an error (`app.css`: "grey, never red"). A freed booking is the same kind of thing.
- **Error red (`{colors.error}`)** appears only in a check-in that failed. It is never used for "freed" or for "nobody has checked in yet".

Avoid introducing green for free or amber for pending. "Keep the app's existing look" rules them out. The status word carries the meaning, and the colour reinforces it.

## Typography

Body, label, meta and title are inherited from `tokens.css`. The door screen adds one ramp of five sizes, all in the app's system-ui stack. `[ASSUMPTION]` These values assume a roughly 10-inch tablet at its default zoom. Check them on the real device from 2–3 m before building.

| Role | Token | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Status | `{typography.door-status}` | "Free", "Booked", "Closed". The largest text on screen. |
| Room | `{typography.door-room}` | The room name, above the status. |
| Current | `{typography.door-current}` | The current or next booking's title, and the Check in label. |
| Detail | `{typography.door-detail}` | Times and the check-in countdown ("Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in"). |
| List | `{typography.door-list}` | Rows in today's list. Read close up. |

My bookings uses the existing ramp. The state tag uses `{typography.label}`.

## Layout & Spacing

The door screen fills the viewport, with no top bar, no tabs, no person and no scroll at the default zoom. `[ASSUMPTION]` The tablet is in landscape.

- **Landscape:** the status panel takes the left ~60%. It holds the room name, status, current booking and the Check in button. Today's list takes the right ~40%. The outer gutter is `{spacing.door-gutter}`.
- **Portrait:** the status panel is on top, with today's list below it. A long list scrolls inside its own column. The status panel never scrolls off the screen.

My bookings keeps its existing layout and gains only a tag line on each booking.

## Elevation & Depth

None, as in the rest of the app. Panels are flat fills with borders.

## Shapes

Inherited: `{rounded.md}` for panels and the Check in button, `{rounded.sm}` for list rows and tags.

## Components

- **Door status panel.** Three variants: `door-status-panel-booked` (navy fill, white text), `door-status-panel-free` (white fill, navy border and text) and `door-status-panel-closed` (grey). Anatomy, top to bottom:
  1. room name in `door-room`
  2. status word in `door-status`
  3. current booking title in `door-current`, with its times in `door-detail`
  4. the countdown line in `door-detail`, when check-in is open
  5. the Check in button

  When the room is free, line 3 becomes "Next: {title} at 14:00" or "Nothing else today".
- **Door Check in button.** Full width of the status panel and `{spacing.door-check-in-height}` tall, more than twice the app's touch target. On the navy panel it is a white button with navy text. That is the app's secondary button inverted, so it stands out on navy without a new colour. The label is "Check in" in `door-current`. While pressed it shows `{colors.navy-tint}`.
- **Checked-in confirmation.** The button is replaced by the line "✓ Checked in" in `door-current`, white on the navy panel. No button remains.
- **Door list item.** One row per booking today: times, then title, then a state word on the right. Variants: current or next booking uses `door-list-item-current` (navy tint), past bookings use `door-list-item-past` (muted ink), the rest use `door-list-item`.
- **Booking state tag (My bookings, details page).** A small label on a booking: "Check in at the door by 10:15", "Checked in" or "Freed: nobody checked in". On the navy organiser link it is white text with no fill. On a freed booking it is muted ink.
- **Freed booking in My bookings.** `calendar-booking-freed`: grey fill with a border and muted ink, so it reads as no longer happening without looking deleted or like an error. The title stays legible and is not struck through.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use navy for booked and white for free, so the screen can be read before any word can | Add green, amber or red for room states |
| Use grey for freed: out of use, not a mistake | Use error red for a freed booking or for "not checked in yet" |
| Keep the room name, status and current booking in the door ramp | Put the list or footer text in the door ramp |
| Use one big Check in button | Add a second action, a confirm step or a who-are-you field next to it |
| Show the status word as well as the panel colour | Let colour alone tell free from booked |

+description: The door tablet's check-in screen and the check-in states of a booking in My bookings. Extends the app's existing tokens (roombooker/static/tokens.css); only the deltas for reading from a distance and the new booking states are new.
+status: final
+created: 2026-11-13
+updated: 2026-11-13
+colors:
+  # Inherited unchanged from roombooker/static/tokens.css. No new colors.
+  navy: '#1B2A4A'
+  navy-hover: '#2A3D66'
+  navy-tint: '#E8ECF4'
+  white: '#FFFFFF'
+  ink: '#1B2A4A'
+  ink-muted: '#5B6474'
+  border: '#D5DAE3'
+  closed: '#F2F3F5'
+  error: '#B42318'
+  error-tint: '#FDECEA'
+typography:
+  # title, body, label, meta inherited from tokens.css (system-ui; 20/16/14/14px).
+  # New: the door ramp, sized for reading from a few steps away on a ~10in landscape tablet. Check on the real device at 2-3 m before building.
+  door-status:
+    fontFamily: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
+    fontSize: 88px
+    fontWeight: '700'
+    lineHeight: '1.0'
+  door-room:
+    fontFamily: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
+    fontSize: 48px
+    fontWeight: '600'
+    lineHeight: '1.1'
+  door-current:
+    fontFamily: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
+    fontSize: 40px
+    fontWeight: '600'
+    lineHeight: '1.2'
+  door-detail:
+    fontFamily: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
+    fontSize: 28px
+    fontWeight: '400'
+    lineHeight: '1.3'
+  door-list:
+    fontFamily: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
+    fontSize: 24px
+    fontWeight: '400'
+    lineHeight: '1.3'
+rounded:
+  sm: 4px
+  md: 8px
+spacing:
+  # 1-6 and touch-target inherited from tokens.css.
+  '1': 4px
+  '2': 8px
+  '3': 12px
+  '4': 16px
+  '5': 24px
+  '6': 32px
+  touch-target: 44px
+  door-gutter: 32px
+  door-check-in-height: 96px
+components:
+  door-status-panel-booked:
+    background: '{colors.navy}'
+    foreground: '{colors.white}'
+    radius: '{rounded.md}'
+  door-status-panel-free:
+    background: '{colors.white}'
+    foreground: '{colors.navy}'
+    border: '{colors.navy}'
+    radius: '{rounded.md}'
+  door-status-panel-closed:
+    background: '{colors.closed}'
+    foreground: '{colors.ink-muted}'
+    radius: '{rounded.md}'
+  door-check-in-button:
+    background: '{colors.white}'
+    foreground: '{colors.navy}'
+    radius: '{rounded.md}'
+    min-height: '{spacing.door-check-in-height}'
+    typography: '{typography.door-current}'
+  door-list-item:
+    background: '{colors.white}'
+    foreground: '{colors.ink}'
+    border: '{colors.border}'
+    radius: '{rounded.sm}'
+  door-list-item-current:
+    background: '{colors.navy-tint}'
+    foreground: '{colors.ink}'
+    radius: '{rounded.sm}'
+  door-list-item-past:
+    foreground: '{colors.ink-muted}'
+  booking-state-tag:
+    background: '{colors.white}'
+    foreground: '{colors.navy}'
+    radius: '{rounded.sm}'
+    typography: '{typography.label}'
+  calendar-booking-freed:
+    background: '{colors.closed}'
+    foreground: '{colors.ink-muted}'
+    border: '{colors.border}'
+    radius: '{rounded.sm}'
+---
+
+## Brand & Style
+
+The door screen is the existing Room Booking app seen from across a corridor. It keeps the app's plain, quiet, navy-and-white look. It adds no new colours, no new typeface and no decoration. The only change is scale. The room name, the word "Free" or "Booked", and the current booking are big enough to read from a few steps away. Everything else on the screen is secondary and can stay small.
+
+The check-in states in My bookings follow the same rule. Each state is a word on the booking, not a new visual language.
+
+## Colors
+
+All colours are inherited from `roombooker/static/tokens.css`. The door screen adds none.
+
+- **Navy (`{colors.navy}`)** fills the status panel when the room is booked. A navy panel or a white one is the cue you can read from furthest away, before any word is legible. Navy keeps its existing meaning: a booking.
+- **White (`{colors.white}`)** with a navy border is the status panel when the room is free. It matches the app's existing free slot (`--slot-free-*`).
+- **Closed grey (`{colors.closed}`)** is the panel for a closed room and the fill for a freed booking in My bookings. The app already uses grey for out of use, not an error (`app.css`: "grey, never red"). A freed booking is the same kind of thing.
+- **Error red (`{colors.error}`)** appears only in a check-in that failed. It is never used for "freed" or for "nobody has checked in yet".
+
+Avoid introducing green for free or amber for pending. "Keep the app's existing look" rules them out. The status word carries the meaning, and the colour reinforces it.
+
+## Typography
+
+Body, label, meta and title are inherited from `tokens.css`. The door screen adds one ramp of five sizes, all in the app's system-ui stack. These values assume a roughly 10-inch tablet at its default zoom. Check them on the real device from 2–3 m before building.
+
+| Role | Token | Used for |
+|---|---|---|
+| Status | `{typography.door-status}` | "Free", "Booked", "Closed". The largest text on screen. |
+| Room | `{typography.door-room}` | The room name, above the status. |
+| Current | `{typography.door-current}` | The current or next booking's title, and the Check in label. |
+| Detail | `{typography.door-detail}` | Times and the check-in countdown ("Freed at 10:15 if nobody checks in"). |
+| List | `{typography.door-list}` | Rows in today's list. Read close up. |
+
+My bookings uses the existing ramp. The state tag uses `{typography.label}`.
+
+## Layout & Spacing
+
+The door screen fills the viewport, with no top bar, no tabs, no person and no scroll at the default zoom. The tablet is in landscape.
+
+- **Landscape:** the status panel takes the left ~60%. It holds the room name, status, current booking and the Check in button. Today's list takes the right ~40%. The outer gutter is `{spacing.door-gutter}`.
+- **Portrait:** the status panel is on top, with today's list below it. A long list scrolls inside its own column. The status panel never scrolls off the screen.
+
+My bookings keeps its existing layout and gains only a tag line on each booking.
+
+## Elevation & Depth
+
+None, as in the rest of the app. Panels are flat fills with borders.
+
+## Shapes
+
+Inherited: `{rounded.md}` for panels and the Check in button, `{rounded.sm}` for list rows and tags.
+
+## Components
+
+- **Door status panel.** Three variants: `door-status-panel-booked` (navy fill, white text), `door-status-panel-free` (white fill, navy border and text) and `door-status-panel-closed` (grey). Anatomy, top to bottom:
+  1. room name in `door-room`
+  2. status word in `door-status`
+  3. current booking title in `door-current`, with its times in `door-detail`
+  4. the countdown line in `door-detail`, when check-in is open
+  5. the Check in button
+
+  When the room is free, line 3 becomes "Next: {title} at 14:00" or "Nothing else today".
+- **Door Check in button.** Full width of the status panel and `{spacing.door-check-in-height}` tall, more than twice the app's touch target. On the navy panel it is a white button with navy text. That is the app's secondary button inverted, so it stands out on navy without a new colour. The label is "Check in" in `door-current`. While pressed it shows `{colors.navy-tint}`.
+- **Checked-in confirmation.** The button is replaced by the line "✓ Checked in" in `door-current`, white on the navy panel. No button remains.
+- **Door list item.** One row per booking today: times, then title, then a state word on the right. Variants: current or next booking uses `door-list-item-current` (navy tint), past bookings use `door-list-item-past` (muted ink), the rest use `door-list-item`.
+- **Booking state tag (My bookings, details page).** A small label on a booking: "Check in at the door by 10:15", "Checked in" or "Freed: nobody checked in". On the navy organiser link it is white text with no fill. On a freed booking it is muted ink.
+- **Freed booking in My bookings.** `calendar-booking-freed`: grey fill with a border and muted ink, so it reads as no longer happening without looking deleted or like an error. The title stays legible and is not struck through.
+
+## Do's and Don'ts
+
+| Do | Don't |
+|---|---|
+| Use navy for booked and white for free, so the screen can be read before any word can | Add green, amber or red for room states |
+| Use grey for freed: out of use, not a mistake | Use error red for a freed booking or for "not checked in yet" |
+| Keep the room name, status and current booking in the door ramp | Put the list or footer text in the door ramp |
+| Use one big Check in button | Add a second action, a confirm step or a who-are-you field next to it |
+| Show the status word as well as the panel colour | Let colour alone tell free from booked |
